posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
If I could go back in time, I would go back in time to the Puritanical English colonies here in America. My reasoning is simple. With some nice close, some facy battery operated gadgets and some medicines and whatnot, I would pretend to be God/Angel, whatever, they were so gullible they'd believe anything (source: Salem Witch Trial). That would be fun. Think about all the stuff I could do that would easily be seen as magic/gods will. I'd probably have to stock up on white clothes though. Pretty sure magic + dark clothes = I end up like Tituba, so I'd have to be very delicate about what I do and say. I probably would have to bring a case of frogs and a case of locusts just in case they didn't believe I was God incarnate, you know, throw a little weight around. Bet they never saw a tuperware container of bullfrogs before. Magic! I could take their pictures with my phone, tell them I have sent a little piece of their soul to Heaven so they wouldn't have to worry about being so damn pious all the time. Gullible, as I said. Playing into their sensibilities would be hard for me at times as I am as secular as they come, but lieing is not hard when there is no possible proof you are lieing. I mean, if I just *poofed* into existence in front of them claiming to be an Angel, what are they gonna do? Prove me wrong? They could cut me or try and kill me I guess, but I'd of course explain that coming to this plane of existence is very risky for me as I take the same form of a Man with all his mortal trappings. 

If that is too much "tampering with History", then the only other real option would be going to Austin Texas, Nov 22 1963. Proving that the US Military Industrial complex staged a coup in this country would be...well it would be something wouldn't it?

posts.cooked:
Nielzabub:

@ Rabit: What theme or type of heroes and villains do you want to see in a future Sentinels expansion. This isn't about what you think is down the pipeline, it's what you want to be down the pipeline.

A family of super-powered, highly-intelligent leporids who are constantly battling for control of the world, to the extent that they suppress each others' efforts enough the people of the world never even notice they are there. Their adventures include villains raiding farms to try to starve out the people, only to have their nemeses route them, smacking them about the head and shoulders with turnips and ruttabegas (before taking a bite of the implements - to keep up their energy to continue the fight against evil, of course). And they never have to worry about running out of allies.


Or, more seriously… That's a challenging question.

I love the fun, positive heroes, but I have Setback and Unity for that. (As much as I prefer stories with positive endings, I get that comics can't do that very easily, as they are supposed to evoke drama and drama doesn't come from the positive, so I don't expect their stories to stay positive all the time.) The next thing would be a villain becoming heroic by choice, by interesting character arc. (Omnitron X doesn't really count as he was programmed; there was no conscious character growth that resulted in him becoming heroic.) Fright Train gave me this, albeit briefly and in an alternate future.

I love time-travel stuff (when it's done well, which I thought Shattered Timelines was) and fantasy-themed material, so I'm set with that.

Thinking about it, almost all the themes and types of characters I really want out of the game (with the exception of positive endings), I already have, so this really is a challenging question.

 

Super-powered leporids it is, then!
